nodes.title: Regime purity is boosts OU predictive performance.
nodes.body: If degenerate observations contaminate the OU regime, emission parameters become biased, reducing forecast quality for non degenerate forecasts. Splitting the non degenerate observations and the degenerate observations, allows for better forecast quality.

nodes.title: Level ambiguity in regime-switching mdoelling approach
nodes.body:
Regime-specific means confound level heterogeneity with dynamic heterogeneity. They do not only capture how the spread behaves, such as fast reversion, slow reversion, or trending. They also capture the absolute level where the spread happened to sit during estimation.

This makes regime labels unstable. A regime identified as "fast mean reversion" may really mean "fast mean reversion around the historical level seen in training." If the spread later shifts to a new level, the model still pulls it toward the old regime level, which may no longer be relevant.

So the regimes partly describe where the spread was, not just how it behaved. This makes the model locally valid but weak out of samp

nodes.title: Avellanda2008 Residual modelling, good candidate for gated learning
Do static factor loadings contaminate the OU residuals?
nodes.body: In the Avellaneda-Lee architecture, factor loadings beta_i are estimated statically (OLS on a fixed window). If the true loadings are time-varying (beta_{i,t}), the observable residual r_{i,t} - beta_i' F_t contains the contamination term (beta_{i,t} - beta_i)' F_t, which is driven by common factors and is not idiosyncratic. Does this contamination bias the OU parameter estimates (kappa, m, sigma)? Can it create spurious apparent mean-reversion or destroy true mean-reversion? This determines how sensitive the downstream HMM is to the upstream factor model's static assumption.

nodes.title: Which upstream factor model is compatible with downstream OU/HMM modelling?
Are factor loadings approximately constant within an HMM regime?
nodes.body: The gated learning idea in C008 assumes that within an OU regime, the factor loadings are stable enough that the PCA-defactored residual is a valid OU process. But if factor loadings drift continuously within a regime (as the DCB and Del Negro-Otrok literature shows they do), the residuals accumulate systematic factor-loading error over the regime duration. This error grows with regime length and common factor volatility. The question is: is the within-regime loading drift small enough to be ignored relative to the idiosyncratic OU signal, or does it materially degrade OU parameter estimates and the gating signal?

Gated Online Learning for Locally Misspecified OU Residual Models:Avellaneda–Lee gives a clean base model for the thesis because it separates stock returns into:

    systematic component + residual component

This is closely related to the cointegration/stat-arbitrage idea: after removing systematic exposure, the remaining residual process is expected to be more stationary or mean-reverting. In Avellaneda–Lee, this residual component is treated as an OU-like mean-reverting process.

This is useful for gated online learning because the residual is not always equally useful for updating the model. Some observations may come from clean mean-reverting behavior, while others may come from local misspecification, unstable beta estimation, high-volume information events, structural drift, or degenerate spread episodes.

The model naturally produces diagnostics that can become gating features:

    1. OU innovations / innovation surprise
    2. volume or trading-time reliability
    3. drift pressure / time-trend effects
    4. beta instability or factor-collinearity
    5. shadow models that indicate whether the current observation fits the assumed OU residual structure

The thesis contribution would be something along the lines of:

    Avellaneda–Lee:
        construct residual -> fit OU -> trade s-score

    Thesis:
        construct residual -> estimate OU/regime state online -> gate or downweight unreliable observations -> improve predictive modelling of the residual process

So the paper gives the deterministic/statistical foundation, while the thesis adds adaptive online learning:

    residual process X_t
        -> online HMM / online EM
        -> learning gate w_t
        -> less learning from degenerate or locally misspecified observations

The strongest connection is their trading-time idea: they already modify signals based on volume, meaning not all observations are treated equally. The thesis generalizes this into a broader learning gate:

    w_t = learning relevance of observation t

where w_t is not only uncertainty, but a heuristic or learned rule for when the model should update strongly, weakly, or not at all.

C008 proposes using AL residuals for gated learning, but this only works if static factor loadings produce valid OU residuals. If time-varying loadings contaminate the residuals, the gating signal is built on a misspecified base.

The claim in C008 requires specifying which factor model sits upstream. The choice of static vs. adaptive vs. regime-specific loadings directly determines whether the OU adequacy criterion and the gating signal are trustworthy.

If factor loadings drift within an HMM regime, the OU residual used for gated learning accumulates loading-estimation error throughout the regime. This directly limits how long a gating window can remain valid before the base residual becomes unreliable.
